name: Side-lying leg raise
movement: the top leg lifted straight up to about forty five degrees and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, facing where your front will be.

words.hint: Lying on your side facing the phone, bottom knee bent, top leg straight and lifted.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your side facing it, bottom knee bent, top leg straight.
words.position: Lie on your side facing the phone, hips stacked one above the other, bottom knee bent for balance, top leg straight in line with your body, toes pointing forward.
words.top: The top leg lifted to about forty five degrees, knee straight, toes still pointing forward, hips still stacked.
howto: Lie on your side facing the phone, head on your arm, bottom knee bent, hips stacked.
Keep the top leg straight and in line with your body — a little behind rather than in front — toes pointing forward, not up at the ceiling.
Lead with the heel and lift the leg to about forty five degrees — no higher: past that the hip hitches and the work leaves the buttock.
Hold for the count, then lower slowly. The rep counts when the leg is back down.
words.cannot: The hips rolling back, the leg drifting forward, and the toes turning up to the ceiling as against pointing away: it sees the lift, the knee and the waist from the front, and reads the foot only by how long it shows. Keep the top hip stacked over the bottom one yourself.
words.about: Side-lying leg raise — lying on your side facing the phone: the lift, as the hip-to-ankle line above level, 30–50° at the top (the hip's own limit is about 45°); the knee at least 160° so the leg stays straight; and the waist kept long — the top shoulder-to-hip length at least 93% of its length at the start, so the hip does not hitch. Hold two seconds at the top, lower slowly, and the rep counts when the leg is back down. During a rep the foot is judged by how long it shows against the shin: pulled back toward you it points at the phone and shows short; past 40% it is pointing away, called but not stopping the count.
words.lost: Lie on your side facing the camera, whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the outside of the hip or the lower back pinches. Keep the movement slow; no swinging.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold.
words.harder: A band around the thighs; an ankle weight; a longer hold.
words.mistakes: Lifting past forty five degrees; hitching the hip toward the ribs; toes turning up; the body rolling back; the leg drifting forward.

measurements.label: shoulder, hip, ankle

settings.label: Lift at the top, at least (degrees above level)
Lift at the top, at most (degrees above level)

measurements.why: The hip-to-ankle line off level: lying with the top leg on the bottom one it reads a little under 0; lifted to about forty five, 30–50. Read from level rather than against the trunk, whose line slopes because the shoulders are wider than the hips. Also the progress measurement.

measurements.label: knee straight

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee kept straight: 180 is locked out. From the front the model reads this knee a few degrees under straight, so the edge is 160.

measurements.label: waist long

settings.label: Top side of the trunk, at least (% of its length at the start)

measurements.why: The top shoulder to the top hip, as a percent of its length at the start: the hip hitching up toward the ribs to lift the leg higher shortens it.

measurements.label: foot length, percent of the shin

settings.label: Foot length against the shin during a rep, at most (percent)

measurements.why: How long the foot is in the picture, as a percent of the shin. Lying face on to the phone, a foot pulled back toward you points its toes at the camera and shows short; a foot pointed along the leg lies in profile and shows long. Past 40 during a rep it is toes pointing away. In a recorded take the raised foot showed 30–45% in most reps and 60–80% when plainly laid along the leg, so 40 calls a foot laid along the leg and lets one only partly pulled back pass; the number is a setting. Read only while the leg is lifted (the gate on lift, under raiseAt): at rest the foot lies however it lies, and the rule is for the rep.
